title: AgentChain
description: v2 (2026-07-29): the CAPABILITY chain for one (agent, model) pair — this backend's source order (agent-supply → sources.order) filtered by eligibility and by 'this source can supply this model, mapping applied'. Deliberately NOT filtered by retry-readiness: a cooling source stays in the chain, dimmed, because the user needs to see it (frame V6 04). The RUNNABLE candidate list of spec §4.3 step 2 is this chain further filtered to `runnable: true`, evaluated per turn — so the two are one definition with one extra filter, not two independent lists. Closes v1's honesty gap: v1 showed one order per agent while N different chains ran underneath it, one per model. Read-only projection, computed per request, never persisted.

model_id.description: The CALLER-FACING menu identifier — the built-in id for fixed-menu backends, the prefixed vendor/model identifier for open menus (never the bare resolved upstream id; see api.md → identifier rules). Mapping is applied inside; the caller does not pre-resolve it.

chain.description: Ordered, position 0 = highest in this backend's order. The next turn uses the FIRST item with `runnable: true`; role is positional and is never stored per source (a source can be serving one agent while merely standing by for another, so `active`/`standby` are not per-chain facts). Rendered with the same order-chip visuals as the agent row (frame V6 01). An EMPTY array is a first-class answer, not an error: the model is in the menu but no eligible source in this backend's order can supply it at all, so the UI flags 无来源可供 (spec §4.6) rather than offering a checkbox that silently fails. A non-empty chain with no `runnable` item is a different thing — see agent-supply `supply_status` (waiting vs interrupted).

via_mapping.description: true when this source supplies the model only because a per-agent mapping rewrote the requested id (spec §4.3 step 1). UI marks the chip 经映射.

resolved_model_id.description: The id actually sent upstream (e.g. glm-5.2 for a requested claude-opus-4-6); null when it equals model_id.

health.description: Source-GLOBAL health, mirrored from source.schema.json → state.status so the chip can dim / gold-dot / flag without a second round trip. Global by design: quota and reachability belong to the account. Note this carries only the health half of that enum — `active`/`standby` are consumption facts and are expressed here by position + `runnable`, never copied per agent.

runnable.description: Whether this candidate is usable right now (health == healthy). false for a cooling or needs_action source: still shown, not tried. This is exactly the retry-readiness filter of spec §4.3 step 2.

retry_at.description: When `runnable` flips back true unattended. Non-null only for health == cooldown; null for needs_action, because nothing recovers without the user.
